ranking_metric: Debian popcon installations (sourcemax/by_inst), maximum over binary packages of the source package
selection: Eight control-verified C++ JSON packages rank by comparable Debian source-package sourcemax installations: JsonCpp 32,707, simdjson 2,688, nlohmann/json 1,799, RapidJSON 899, Glaze 171, PicoJSON 16, jsoncons 3, and taoJSON 2. Boost.JSON 1.92.0 is verified but primary-unranked because its Debian source covers all of Boost; it is kept under PROTOCOL.md's fallback by its JSON-specific libboost-json-dev count (1,749). POCO JSON 1.15.4 was verified but demoted: its only counts are suite-wide (libpoco-dev 190) or below the 1,000 fallback (libpocojson100 125). Nine of ten slots are used.
uncertainty: Nine C++ JSON package paths pass two valid controls with scoped parser source coverage and stable AFL++ feedback. Glaze uses a generic_i64 DOM and a parser-only probe; jsoncons uses the insertion-ordered ojson tree and a parser-only probe whose AFL++ allowlist names the basic_json_parser methods, because a file-only allowlist dropped parser functions whose first instruction is inlined from another header; PicoJSON and taoJSON use the same function-scoped allowlist approach. PicoJSON and taoJSON store objects in std::map, so their trees lose source key order: their controls check array order and integer/float kinds exactly but compare object members by key. taoJSON runs its own grammar on the separately pinned PEGTL 3.2.6 engine, and its 1.0.0-beta.14 tag is an upstream pre-release; no final 1.0.0 exists. The lowest ranks rest on weak signals: PicoJSON 16 installations (0 recent), jsoncons 3 (1 recent), and taoJSON 2 (both no_files). Glaze has 171 comparable Debian source-package installations, but the source metric favors runtime packages and undercounts header-only libraries. Boost.JSON has no JSON-specific Debian source count and is kept by its 1,749 JSON-specific dev installs. POCO JSON passed the technical gate but was demoted for lack of a qualifying metric (data/cpp/json/poco-json-demoted.json). One documentation lead remains unresolved: Qt. The 320 JSON-name source hits exclude Glaze, found by a supplementary exact source-name lookup. No complete top-ten claim follows. Two small valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259, numeric boundaries, other encodings, or malformed-input behavior.
